blocks.content: The Food Corporation of India was setup under the Food Corporation Act 1964, in order to fulfill the objectives of the Food Policy.

rows: Strategic reserve for emergency shortages and price stabilization
Regular monthly distribution through PDS and welfare schemes
Maintained for long-term food security emergencies

items: FCI was formally inaugurated on 14th January 1965 at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu.
MSP is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and approved by CCEA.
Buffer stock norms for foodgrains are fixed quarterly by the Government of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: FCI was established under the Food Corporation Act, 1964 to execute the national food policy.
Main objectives include providing price support to farmers, distributing foodgrains via PDS, and maintaining strategic reserves.
Procurement of foodgrains is undertaken at Minimum Support Price (MSP) announced by the Central Government.
FCI plays a central role in managing food security through buffer stock management and inter-state movement of grains.
